reviews.review_description: “Anton Hand hears from players from time to time who want to shoot humans in the hot dog games. People ask for this because they recognize the most immersive gun handling ever developed. What they don’t recognize is that VR is different from traditional games and we experience it differently. Having a good time in simulation doesn’t mean having the most immersive murder simulator. It means creating a gun club or shooting range that has all the benefits of virtual reality. H3VR2 shows you can have a great time alone just beating meat.” - @goodvirtualreality dot com

The best gun handling I've experienced in a standalone Quest game. Every grip, reload, shot and sound feels fantastic, and there's a great variety of weapons and attachments. It looks amazing and ran smoothly on my Quest 3, even while recording.

The Facility's extraction loop is addictive: fight Sosigs, extract loot, recycle it and upgrade for future runs. It's challenging even on the lowest difficulty, and the early weapons and economy could use some balancing. The shooting challenges and sandbox are great fun too.

My biggest issue was losing control during fights. My pistol sometimes stopped responding until I released and grabbed it again, and my character occasionally kept moving forward after I let go of the stick while force-grabbing. This happened often and cost me many runs. This issue appears to be happening only to me, and I don't know whether the game or my controller is responsible.

Even so, this is a fantastic VR shooter.

My full review is on my YouTube channel ‘Gamertag VR’ 
Hot Dogs, Horseshoes & Hand Grenades 2 surprised me. I never cared for the original sandbox, but the new extraction-shooter campaign is frustratingly addictive. Brutal trial and error, realistic weapons, risky loot decisions and a genuine sense of discovery kept me coming back. Yes, you’re fighting hotdogs, and somehow it works! The Quest visuals and performance impress, though PCVR will likely look better. If you enjoy challenging solo shooters, I recommend it.Use code GTVR for 10% off.

reviews.review_title: THANK YOU FOR NOT BEING BEYOND SANDBOX
reviews.review_description:
You guys are genuinely the best, I’ve been following the h3vr2 devlogs for a while now and being able to play it has been AMAZING, I haven’t done much yet but I plan on playing a lot more now that it’s available.

Anyway, they did basically everything right that I wanted and was hoping for. The guns are so fun to use and feel pretty realistic. Handling magazines is super fun and they added a bunch of neat details like being able to mess up cocking a sniper by not putting the charging handle all the way down causing it to not fire but still lets you pull the trigger. 

This game is definitely the better out of the two in my opinion as while the first game definitely is more detailed and has more content (as of now), h3vr2 has more lore, more physical interactivity and much more to actually keep you interested in the game besides shooting guns.

On the topic of the game, hands make take and hold 10x better since not only does it make everything a lot more easier to see and understand much better than the old holo hands. A huge problem I had with the old take and hold was how repetitive the old system was, it felt a bit intense to shoot the crystals while under fire from 7 different points so making the game much more “exploration”filled is definetely much appreciated. The ai is pretty good and is surprisingly challenging, it’s nice they didn’t hire a bunch of weenies this time around.

I even did a stress test of the game by spawning in thousands of shotgun shells and throwing them at a wall, while slowdown was obviously evident it still held up incredibly well.

I only have 2 real problems with the game 

-The gravity of throwing things and tossing items around feels a bit floaty

- Atms do not allow you to deposit coins ( They glitch around in your hand when they get close to the coin slot and play the sound of them being inserted at like 1000 rpm)

-The only preorder bonus I managed to get was the horseshoe and the tippy toy, I dunno if it’s a bug or something but frankly this one doesn’t bother me that much

Besides theses things I really have no problems with this game

Keep doing what you guys love, cuz I LOVE IT TOO

First and foremost, this is extraction shooter forward. While the sandbox is fun, H3VR2 is heavily focused on the extraction shooter gamemode, which may put off those who enjoyed H3VR1 for its decent distribution of features across all gamemodes. The game is fairly difficult at first, but is insanely rewarding when you get the hang of it. I will miss a few features from the old installment, but overall it's a great time, which is surprising as I don't typically enjoy extraction shooters.

I already adore the game completely. To say it's a straight upgrade from the first game would be a massive understatement. However, I am in desperate need of joystick deadzone settings due to the stick drift that my left controller has. It makes it nearly impossible to play and aim at the same time, constantly sliding all over the place.

This is extremely polished compared to the first one.

I mean, it really has impressed me.

You really owe it to yourself. Give it a chance.

reviews.review_title: H3VR2 - The best VR game on the market

reviews.review_title: The BEST VR Guns & Extraction Shooter
reviews.review_description:
Rust LTD. has done it once again. The most realistic and interactive firearms in VR is back, bigger, badder and better than ever! Anton did not bait a single feature in his devlogs, and it truly is a next gen VR title with what they've accomplished.

The content at launch is extremely generous and will keep you occupied for a long time. The challenge courses are fun and varied and The Facility (the main extraction story mode) is like a challenging puzzle for you to solve. This game is so worth the wait and so worth the price. Highly recommend!!

Are you a gun nerd? Yes? Then play this game.  the gun simulation will simply blow your mind, just to give you a taste, All of the guns have real-time simulation for the ballistics and springs meaning if it can happen in real life, good chance it can happen in this game, and btw this game has the most realistic sound library out. Your ears will thank you

reviews.review_title: Everything it was promised to be.
reviews.review_description:
The control is sublime, every interaction is dialed-in, yet fluid.
The feedback for everything from loose objects, to the most integral parts-the GUNS, is so delightfully smooth and clean, it quite literally puts everything else on the platform to shame by comparison.

The only way it could be bested, would be H3VR1 to be available on the platform, and even then, I'd be saying "Can we get some reverse engineering done to get these physics and interactions up to speed with the sequel?".
That's probably the highest praise I have ever felt a game has ever deserved, and all I can say, is that I'm looking forward to seeing this base expounded upon, and watching it grow from here!

(Maybe, hopefully, including the original T&H getting revamped for this as a crossover mode?
That'd be absolutely WONDERFUL, to quote the man himself, Anton (Madman) Hand.)

The game, CURRENTLY, just doesn't feel all that good to play. Enemies and NPCs losing their minds over a small and unintentional shoulder check (when they're crowding the hallway), the little blade drones rushing you for no clear reason where no other drone would, ATMs (for me, at least) entirely not working or allowing coins to pass beyond their gates, just about every weapon I've tried feeling like a stapler against even the most basic enemies, and inventory management that feels sort of frustrating when trying to grab a specific item in the middle of other items. All that being said, I know these developers, and I know this game will reach perfection. Unfortunately though, it just isn't quite there yet.

I can tell Anton and the rest of the developers have worked very hard to make this game as perfect as it is, the first game was already way ahead of its time but this the second one is just incredible its a bit confusing at first but its honestly a great game. Props to him and the rest of the team.

reviews.review_title: Totally Lives up to the expectations
reviews.review_description:
I’ve always wanted to play the OG H3VR but never had a computer capable of streaming to my quest where it was playable so when I saw the sequel was coming to quest 3 standalone I was so pumped and it was the only vr game I was excited to play and only time I’veever preordered a vr game. And its been great so far in my short time of playing and it’s certainly delivered on its promises that Anton and the team have been showing on their YouTube page. 

Sure the game might feel a little empty especially if you’re familiar with the huge gun and attachment library from the first game but it’s only day one and we all know the devs will be adding in so much more over time. Also I love how its not a huge heavy game that takes up most of the storage so you have to delete lots of stuff in your library in order to accommodate like a lot of shooters on the store so that’s a huge win for this game 
 
My only little gripe is that I wish there was an option to choose whether the gun has weight or not because I personally enjoy a little more arcadey weightless gunplay personally but that’s not a criticism of the game at al. But I think this game is definitely worth the price
